rows.title_short: The Philippine Veterinary Medicine Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"The Philippine Veterinary Medicine Act of 2003\". Animals and their by-products are potential carriers of diseases. They are often the source of diseases transmissible to man. Therefore, it is imperative that to regulate the profession entrusted tomanage the country's animal health. This measure seeks to upgrade the practice of veterinary medicine for the purpose of protecting the animal population in the country. It aims to uplift the role of veterinarians in safeguarding public health and inthe control of zoonotic diseases.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY COUNCIL AND PROVIDING POWERS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Emergency Health Powers Act".  In the light of new and emerging threats, including emergent and resurgent infectious diseases and terrorists attacks involving the use of chemical, biological or nuclear agents, it is a must that a set plan is established to counteract such emergence or resurgence of contagion. This bill seeks to create a Public Health Emergency Council which would have the primary responsibility to draw up a battle plan against a public health emergency and implement the same.It aims to give us a fighting chance against biological, chemical or nuclear health threats through preparation, management and disposal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-05-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT HARMONIZING AND RATIONALIZING THE ADMINISTRATION AND GRANT OF FISCAL AND NON-FISCAL INCENTIVES REPEALING FOR THIS PURPOSE EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS CODE OF 1987
rows.title_short: The Investments and Incentives Code of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"The Investments and Incentives Code of the Philippines\". This bill will result to one governing stature regulating the grant of incentives by all investment promotion agencies of the government. It will harmonize and simplify the administration offiscal and non-fiscal incentives to promote foreign and domestic investments. It proposes a clear, simple, time-bound, performance-bas ed and competitive set of incentives comparable with those of other countries in the region. It also offers new incentives like the 12-year income tax holiday for certain kinds of projects or an option to avail of the net operating loss carry-over or accelerated depreciation. It provides for a shortened processing period of application, registration and getting oof clearance, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT REVISING THE START OF THE SCHOOL CALENDAR FROM JUNE THROUGH MARCH TO SEPTEMBER THROUGH MAY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7797, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Typhoons generally visit the country from June to August. During the period, students are exposed to the hazards brought about by floods, traffic, landslides, and water-borne diseases outbreak, among others. School buildings are also used as evacuation and health centers during floods. This measure proposes to revise the school schedule by moving the start of the school calendar, gradually, from June to September. This would spare students from the hazards brought about by typhoons.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-05-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING THE AMOUNT OF ONE BLLION PESOS (P1,000,000,000 .00) FROM THE AGGREGATE EARNINGS OF THE PHILIPPINE AMUSEMENT AND GAMING CORPORATION FOR THE MAINTENANCE OPERATION OF THE PHILIPPINE DRUG ENFORCEMENT AGENCY
rows.abstract: The drug problem in the country has reached alarming proportions. It now affects the whole nation.  This bill provides for an additional funding of PhP 1.0 billion for the maintenance and operation of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA). The fund shall be sourced from the aggregate gross earnings of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation. This would enable the PDEA to effectively carry out its programs and projects to combat the drug menace.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-05-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY INCOME BENEFITS FOR WORK-RELATED PERMANENT DISABILITY AND DEATH OF WORKERS AND EMPLOYEES
rows.abstract: To protect the spendable income of workers and pensioners from the ill-effects of world-wide inflation, actuarial studies must be undertaken with a view to upgrading the income benefits for work-related permanent disability and death of workers andemployees. This measure proposes an additional 25% across-the-boar d increase in the monthly income benefits for work-related permanent disabilities and death of employees, without requiring additional premium contributions from the employers and employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-05-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE PERIOD FROM MAY 1 TO 7 OF EVERY YEAR AS THE NATIONAL OLDER WORKERS WEEK
rows.abstract: Our work force is dominated by older workers who have rendered invaluable service not only the companies they work for but to the society as well. However, their immeasurable contributions have not been given due recognition. The bill proposes to declare the period from May to May 7 of every year as the "National Older Workers Week" to give due recognition to the contributions given by workers, both in the government and in the private sectors, aged fifty years and above.  A nationwide search for outstanding older workers in various categories shall be conferred with honorary and cash awards.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-05-21

rows.abstract: "Environmental Planning Practice Act". The measure provides a more responsive and comprehensive regulation for the registration, licensing and practice of Environmental Planning in the light of local and international developments in the field. It provides for a more precise definition of the practice of Environmental Planning.  It seeks to regulate the practice of foreign Environmental Planning, including the issuance of Special/Tempora ry Permits, when applicable. The measure also proposes aContinuing Professional Education (CPE) to make professional globally competitive.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF LIVE OR DEAD PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES
rows.title_short: Prohibiting the Detention of Live or Dead Patients in Hospitals on the Grounds of Nonpayment of Bills
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to prevent the undesirable practice of hospitals and medical clinics of preventing the release of fully recovered or dead patients due to non-payment of hospital/medica l bills.  This practice results in a prolonged and more expensivestay in the hospital of financially distressed patients. Said detention, in a sense, constitutes a deprivation of liberty on the grounds of financial incapacity. This bill allows underprivileged patients to leave the hospital upon the execution of aduly secured (either by mortgage or by a guarantee of a co-maker) promissory note.  It also imposes a penal sanction for any violation of the proposed act.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-08-04, transmitted to on 2003-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2003-08-07

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Notes of HB Nos. 47 and 4910 as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS TO UTILIZE ALL ITS INCOME FOR THEIR MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Authorizing Government Hospitals to Utilize its Income for Maintenance
rows.abstract: The practice of disallowing government hospitals from spending their income for maintenance and other operating expenses restricts their ability to respond to the needs of their clients. It also dampens the initiative of the hospital adminstrator toexpand and improve their services. This is perceived to be one of the reasons why government hospitals are unable to deliver adequate and timely health services. Utilization of their income can augment the budget appropriated to them by the nationalor local government. The bill provides that government hospitals shall be authorized to utilize income derived from pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, operating room, nursery and other facilities plus income derived from non-patient related services ffor maintenance and other operating expenses including capital outlay.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-08-04, transmitted to on 2003-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2003-08-07

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of HB Nos. 364 and 1517 as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C069
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF MINING ENGINEERING IN THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 4274
rows.abstract: "Philippine Mining Engineering Act of 2003". The Mining Engineering Law (RA 4274) which was enacted in 1965, urgently needs to be amended and updated to make the law more realistic and relevant to the current practice of Mine Engineers in the country.  The bill seeks to promote and recognize the importance of the Mining Engineering profession in nation-building .  It underscores the need to develop competent, globally competitive and well-rounded Mining Engineers through regulatory measures, programs and activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-05-26

rows.author: C101
rows.title_full: AN ACT REORGANIZING THE NATIONAL FOOD AUTHORITY INTO THE NATIONAL FOOD CORPORATION, REDEFINING ITS POWERS AND CREATING THE FOOD DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ADMINISTRATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Food Authority Reorganization of 2003".  The National Food Authority (NFA) is mandated to ensure food security in staple cereals during calamities and emergencies, and stability of staple cereal supply and prices. However, for as long as farmers do not have easy and adequate access to irrigation, affordable credit, low-price farm inputs, basic post harvest facilities and reliable structures like farm-to-market roads, food security in staple cereals through self-sufficienc y will be difficult to achieve. To enable the NFA to meet its mandate, this bill proposes to strengthen the NFA financially and structurally so it will develop into a strong Food Development and Regulatory Administration and a State Trading Enterprise.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-05-26

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NEW LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "New Labor Code of the Philippines". The proposed labor code reinforces the narrow orientation of the Constitution to afford full protection to labor based on employer- employee relationship. It seeks to achieve the following objectives, among others:>>a) to provde for a more effective regulation of recruitment and placement activities with the restoration of the regulatory functions of the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration; >>b) to ensure humane conditions of work - increase the service incentive leave from 5 to 10 days, grant male workers paternity leave of 7 days with pay and grant the right to family and medical leave of 4 weeks without pay every every year when the worker and his family is suffering from serious illness;>>> and c) to afford workers the fullest possible exercise of their constitutional rights to self-organizati on, collective bargaining, peaceful concerted activities and the right to strike according to law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2003-05-26

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7392, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE MIDWIFERY ACT OF 1992, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Midwifery has a significant role in the health care and education, not only of pregnant women, but also their family and community. The midwife, aside from caring and assisting in childbirth, has additional roles, such as educator community resourceand leader, and advocate for the health and well-being of women and children. However, midwives and their role in the central care of women remain unrecognized and unappreciated. This bill intends to professionalize the practice of midwifery - strengthen its education and training through a revision of the standard curriculum and through a midwifery continuing education. It also provides for more work opportunities through the step-ladder approach to midwifery education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-06-02

rows.author: D076
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENSURING SECURITY OF TENURE FOR AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES OVER LANDS AWARDED TO THEM UNDER THE COMPREHENSIVE AGRARIAN REFORM PROGRAM, PROVIDING GUIDELINES FOR THE CANCELLATION OF LAND OWNERSHIP AWARDS, PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: There is an alarming number of cancellations of Emancipation Patents (EPs) and Certificates of Land Ownership Awards (CLOAs) issued to farmer beneficiaries under the land reform program of the government. These cancellations were mainly because thesubject pieces of land were erroneously covered under PD 27 and Ra 6657. Many EPS and CLOAs were canceled even after the farmer beneficiaries have paid the required amortization for the lands awarded to them. This bill seeks to reaffirm that EPs andCLOAs are land titles under PD 1529. It provides the prescriptive period for the filing of petition for the cancellation of EP and CLAOs. It also provides for compensation to landowners whose lands were erroneously covered by land reform programs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2003-06-02

rows.author: D020
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SENIOR CITIZENS TECHNOLOGY AND LIVELIHOOD CENTER IN EVERY BARANGAY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: To maximize the role of senior citizens in nation building, the government must adopt measures whereby senior citizens are assisted and appreciated by the community for their contributions. This measure seeks to provide the elderly with services inthe form of actual teaching, demonstration and transfer of new skills and expand the opportunities for gainful senior citizens to find employment through available technology and livelihood programs. It proposes to establish a Senior Citizens Technology and Livelihood Center in every barangay.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A TOTAL BAN ON ANTI-PERSONNEL LANDMINES, FOR OTHER PROHIBITIONS OR RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF LANDMINES, BOOBY-TRAPS AND OTHER DEVICES, FOR CREATION OF A PHILIPPINE COORDINATING COMMITTEE ON LANDMINES, AND FOR RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Philippine Comprehensive Law on Landmines". In compliance with our obligations under the Ottawa Treaty (1997 Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on Their Destruction) and the Amended Protocol II (1996 Amended Protocol on Prohibition or Restrictions on the Use of Mines, Booby Traps and Other Devices) which we ratified, the Philippines is obliged to take all appropriate legislative and other measures to implement these treaties. This bill proposes the following among others: (1) the adoption of a total ban on anti-personnel mines; (b) the application of the total ban on anti-personnel mines to their transit and carrying by visiting foreign military vessels and forces, inncluding in joint military exercises, in Philippine territory; and (c) a ban on technology transfer regarding anti-personnel mines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2003-06-02

rows.abstract: "National Transportaiton Safety Act of 2002". The importance and necessity of a safe transportation system in the country cannot be overemphasized. This measusre proposes the creation of the National Transportation and Safety Board (NTSB), which shall be an independent and non-regulatory agency taske to ensure thorough and impartial investigations of transporation accidents. rows.title_full: AN ACT CONSOLIDATING ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME LAWS TO MODERNIZE THE MARITIME INDUSTRY, PROMOTE AND REGULATE MERCHANT MARINE ACTIVITIES, RATIONALIZE THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME MATTERS, AND INSURE THE PROTECTION OF THE MARINE WEALTH IN THE PHILIPPINE TERRITORY
rows.abstract: "Maritime Administration Act of 2001". At present, the maritime administration functions of the government are spread over fourteen bureaus and agencies under seven departments resulting in bureaucratic entanglement, functional overlaps and conflicting laws and regulations. This bill aims to put an end to the fragmentation and overlapping of functions in the different government agencies and create a body that will be the central agency concerned with maritime administration. It seeks to solvethe multifarious problems plaguing the administration of the maritime sector.

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ORDAIN AND INSTITUTE THE MARITIME CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: "Maritime Code of the Philippines". The laws governing the relations between and among the parties and interests in maritime commerce and trade to and from the Philippines are dispersed in various codes, laws, decrees, executive and order and treaties. This bill seeks to update and reform the shipping laws of the country and codify the same into one code. It upgrades the laws dealing with registration of ships, maritime liens and ship mortgages, maritime fraud, accident at sea and shipowner's liability. It provides for a separate common carrier provision to apply specifically to ships or vessels transporting passengers and/or goods, domestically or internationally . Likewise, it updates the marine insurance provisions found in the Insurancce Code of 1978 and juxtaposes such provisions alongside other provisions of admiralty and maritime laws. The bill also provides for an alternative dispute settlement in the form of arbitration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2003-06-04

rows.abstract: "The Public Infrastructure Billboard Act of 2003". In line with the government's policy of public disclosure in all its transactions involving public interest, the bill seeks to make transparent every public transaction involving public infrastructure projects. It requires public contractors to put up a public information board indicating the cost and expenditure of the infrastructure project. This policy of transparency would serve as a deterrent to the commission of any irregularity.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING DOMESTIC VIOLENCE, PROVIDING PROTECTION MEASURES AND PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES (RA09262 - 03/08/2004 enacted together with HB05516 & SB02723)
rows.title_short: The Anti-Domestic Violence Act
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Domestic Violence Act\". Taking cognizance of the worsening incidence of domestic violence as both a social ill and a cime that needs to be decisively addressed with appropriate laws, policies, programs and services for its arrest, prevention and eliminatin; the bill defines the crime of domestic violence and imposes stiff penalties on perpetrators of the crime to enable the State to guarantee the safety and security of the individual members of the family. It provides a comprehensive package of ample protection to victims and survivors of domestic violence through the grant of immediate and other necessary relief including the issuance of protection orders (POs). It also details the procedures for the issuance and availment of POs annd the filing of domestic criminal complaints.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR EXEMPTION FROM INCOME TAX THE QUALIFIED INCIDENTAL EXPENSES INCURRED BY TEACHERS RELATIVE TO THEIR PROFESSION
rows.abstract: "Teacher Tax Relief Act of 2003". Teachers play a vital role in nation-building . They mold the minds of the youth to prepare them to become socio-civic minded citizens. However, they are forced to seek jobs abroad because their take home pay locally is not enough to meet the financial requirements of their families. In order to lessen the financial burden of teachers and prevent their exodus abroad, this bill seeks to exempt from income taxation the qualified incidental expenses incurred by teachers relative to their profession. The qualified incidental expenses shall include personal expenses for books, supplies, equipment and other materials needed in their teaching activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-06-05

rows.abstract: "The Land Administration Reform Act of 2003". The performance of government agencies in undertaking land surveys, mapping, classification, disposition and registration is hampered by fundamental legal and institutional defects in both the structureand operations of the land administration system. These defects have lead to inefficiencies and delays in the disposition and titling of alienable and disposable lands, inaccurate and incomplete land records, and duplicate and fake titles. This billproposes to consolidate the land administration powers and functions currently dispersed to the Department of Justice's Land Administration Authority and Register of Deeds; and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' Land Management Bureeau, Land Management Services, National Mapping and Resource Information Authority and the CARP Secretariat, with the creation of the Land Administration Authority (LAA). The LAA shall be the primary agency responsible for land administration and pub

rows.abstract: "Philippine Cultural Heritage Law of 2003". The Philippines has a rich cultural heritage. However, many of these are in the verge of ruin due to their prolonged exposure to natural wear and tear and the lack of attention being given them. This billseeks to protect, preserve, conserve and promote the nation's cultural heritage, its properties and its histories in order to conserve the ethnicity of local communities and of the nation as a whole. It also aims to establish and strengthen culturalinstitutions and to protect cultural workers and assure their professional development and well-being.

rows.abstract: "Anti-Rebies Act of 2002". Rabies, a fatal viral disease affecting the nervous system, remains a public health problem in the country. Approximately 300 to 450 Filipinos die of rabies every year. The bill provides for the implementation of a Nationwide Rabies Prevention and Control Program to be undertaken by the Departments of Agriculture, Health, Interior and Local Government and Education as well as by local government units with the assistance of non-government organizations. The Program aims to eliminate rabies and eventually declare the Philippines rabies-free.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING CERTAIN TOURISM-ORIENTE D ESTABLISHMENTS AND TOURIST WORKERS TO SECURE ACCREDITATION FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM AS A PREREQUISITE TO THE ISSUANCE OF LICENSE OR PERMIT TO OPERATE BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.title_short: Requiring Tourism-Oriented Establishments and Tourist Workers to Secure Accreditation from the Department of Toruism
rows.abstract: In line with the primary thrust of government of develop and promote the Philippines as a world-class tourist destination and venue for international conventions, tourism establishments and tourist workers shall be required to maintain the minimum standards set forth in the rules and regulations promulgated by the Department of Tourism (DOT) based on international levels of quality and efficiency. The measure proposes to require tourism-oriente d establishments and tourist workers to secure accreditation from the DOT as a prerequisite to the issuance of license, permit to operate or conduct business relative to tourism. It also seeks the creation of an Accreditation and Monitoring Committee in all provinces, cities and municipalities whichh shall evaluate tourism establishments and workers for purposes of accreditation.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-11-19, transmitted to on 2003-11-20 and received by the Senate on 2003-12-01

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Notes of the original House Bills No. 3190 and 4995 as the sponsorship remarks.
